rows.Incident Item Name: OLD-A female guest standing outside the room
rows.Incident Description:
- SRC PD2C, Ms. Cho, Siu Ngan Joanne, CCMASCL1, staying on 31Dec-4Jan.
- At around 08:10hrs, Ms. Wu King (Rm#3710, SRC PD3B) came to FO counter and claimed she found one unknown elderly lady in 37F. The elderly lady seemed need assistance. FOGRO thanked for Ms. Cho’s feedback. Guest had no further pursue and left for breakfast.
- At 08:27hrs, Security received emergency request from Facility to check Back of House Lift S07 on 37F to check if any elderly guest entered. Security found one elderly lady in Back of House Lift on 37F then escorted to Conrad Lobby for further assistance.
- The elderly lady was around 80 years and forgot her room number, she provided three mobile phone numbers which HFO had contacted but in vain. The lady mentioned stayed with her husband and daughter.
rows.Subject: CN 73718 | Ms. Cho Siu Ngan Joanne | One elderly female guest lost her way in 37F
rows.Investigation/Follow Up 1: OLD-A female guest standing outside the room
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
- FOSUP contacted Rm#3718 and main guest Ms. Cho went to Conrad Lobby,  accompanied the elderly lady back to Rm#3718. Ms. Cho did not disclose the details of the elderly lady.
- Rooms had been affected:
1. Rm#3710: Ms. Wu King ,  SRC PD3B,  staying on 31Dec – 1Jan. Ms. Wu express checked-out already.
2. Rm#3704: Mr. Yang Jianjun,  SRC PD3C,  staying on 31Dec-2Jan. At 10:22hrs,  Mr. Yang called to request smoking room without mentioning knocking door by unknown guest. FOGRO assisted guest room move from 3704 to 605. 
- Case shared with PSC and HSKP teams.
- HFO will monitor other guests’ feedback of disturbance by knocking doors by the elderly lady.
- HFO will see off guests upon departure.
rows.Investigation/Follow Up 2: OLD-A female guest standing outside the room
rows.Investigation Remarks 2:
- Security team check the CCTV and according to CCTV footage:
1. At 08:02hrs,  the elderly lady came out from Conrad room 3718 and approached to Conrad room 3717 & 3719 but cannot confirmed if she knocked the door or rang the doorbell.
2. At 08:04hrs,  the elderly lady approached to Conrad room 3718.
3. 08:05hrs,  she approached to Conrad room 3710.
4. At 08:06hrs,  she approached to Conrad room 3704 and tried to open the door.
5. At 08:09hrs,  she approached to Conrad room 3705.
6. At 08:11hrs,  she approached to Conrad room 3717.
7. At 08:12hrs,  1 female guest of Conrad room 3710 found the elderly lady standby at outside Conrad room 3717.
8. At 08:15hrs,  she followed the guest to L37 Guest lift lobby then left respectively.
9. At 08:21hrs,  she entered BOH lift S07 at L37 then pressed the emergency button.
10. At 08:28hrs,  the lift door was closed and she was at L37 BOH lift lobby. 
11. At 08:33hrs,  Security arrived and assisted her to L1 Conrad FO lobby.

rows.Incident Description:
FIT Ms. Shi Zihan, Mr. Shi Jianguo (father) and Mr. Li, Li (mother), Ctrip booking, Total MOP 1925.58, Staying on 4-6 Jan, 2026.
- At 23:11hrs, guest contacted PSC and claimed there was no power of sockets. PSC sent job to Facility for follow up.
- At 23:20hrs, guest contacted PSC again and chased to fix the power issue.
- At 23:33hrs, guest requested to talk with manager.
- HFO extended courtesy call to Ms. Shi and learnt as below:
1. Her farther Mr. Shi used kettle and found it was stopping heating water. 
2. Her mother used hotel hair dryer found there was no power in all sockets in room.
3. She felt very convenient that in the late evening and affected their rest.
4. She preferred Conrad brand and chose us for celebrating parents’ 40th Wedding Anniversary.
- HFO did sincere apology for inconvenience caused and showed appreciation for guest’s choosing us to stay. During conversation, Facility team had fixed the power tripped issue.
- Learnt guest’s room package was not including breakfast and invited guests for breakfast in Churchill’s Table as courtesy. 
- Guests will go to Zhuhai after check-out and late check-out arranged at 12:00hrs as courtesy.
- GR team prepared anniversary cake and initial bears as gifts during their stay.
- Ms. Shi thanked for our prompt follow-up and noted to contact us for any further assistance.
- HFO will meet guests during breakfast and see off guests upon departure.
rows.Subject: 72416 | Ms. Shi Zihan | Power Tripped in Conrad RM2416
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
-At 12:00 HSKPHOD received call by FOSUP,  Room 2416 tripped again when guest using kettle. After guest C/O,  HSKP raised an order to FAC or repair.
-HSKP also checked the kettle and the base,  suspected the water leaked from the kettle into the base,  causing a short circuit and triggering the circuit breaker. HSKP has replaced new kettle in the room.
rows.Investigation Remarks 2:
- At 11:45hrs,  FO SUP was informed by PSC that Ms. Shi feedback the power tripped again when she uses the kettle. 
- As Ms. Shi mentioned they about to leaving,  PSC offered to deliver hot water to the room by IRD team asap which accepted by Ms. Shi.
- FO SUP courtesy called to the room and sincerity apologized to the guest. During the phone conversation,  Ms. Shi feedback to FO SUP that she really disappointed that the power tripped again and affected her stay experience. 
- FO SUP learned that guest depart from Hengqin at around 12:30hrs with heavy luggage as they bought a lot of souvenirs. FO SUP further provided departure limo to Hengqin (Macao) as courtesy.
- At 12:25hrs,  FO SUP escorted Ms. Shi and her family to the limousine with luggage assistance. Ms. Shi thanked for our follow up.

rows.Incident Description:
	At about 1420hrs, GSH Carl was informed by PSC that Ms. You, who checked out from Conrad hotel room 2411 this morning, reported one pocket on her backpack was opened by unknown person and one brown wallet inside was missing when her luggage was kept in the luggage room. A photograph of the black backpack is attached for your reference. 

	Firstly, GSH Carl and GS Supervisor John searched the area where her luggage was stored in the luggage room, but no such item was found. Secondly, hotel L&F and shuttle bus team also assisted to check but negative findings. Thirdly, Surveillance department also confirmed no one had approached her luggage during the storage period and the said pocket was zipped up all the time from the moment the luggage was handed to GS team until they departed via MIA shuttle bus. 

	Ms. You complained this caused a lot of trouble, she only mentioned she had to report credit card missing to her bank, but she did not mention anything else in that wallet.  

	At about 1614hrs, GSH Carl communicated the findings to Ms. You through WhatsApp. And Ms. Yu replied at 1910hrs with the message below. 

	“Thank you for checking. But I don’t think u need to check the shuttle because my daughter and I were sitting together & I was holding my backpack with me in the seat. My wallet was in the same small pocket on the bag, and there were my passport & other papers too. But only the wallet went missing. Anyways, thank you again for your support. I think you have done enough to help me.”

	Ms. Yu’s emotion scale is about 8. 

	Security CCTV email reply as below
On 10/Jan
1123hrs, the guests approached and stored 2x luggage and 1x black backpack at Londoner Luggage Counter
1127hrs, the 3x items were placed near the luggage rack in the Luggage Room
1332hrs, Concierge TM approached and moved the 3x items out from Luggage Room
1333hrs, the guests took back 2x luggage and 1x black backpack from Concierge
1335hrs, the guest carried the backpack on his shoulders when he was queuing at the Shuttle Bus Queue
1342hrs, they boarded a Shuttle Bus at West Lobby Drop Off (Route: Macau International Airport)

During the review in the Luggage Room between 1127hrs and 1332hrs, the zipper of the black backpack was zipped. Nobody approached the guests’ items.
Before the male guest boarded the Shuttle Bus at 1342hrs, the bag was still zipped up and no suspicion was found.
Ref#26015-1075

rows.Incident Description:
At 09:36 on 11Feb26, received a complaint email from Mr. Kang details as below:

1. Room condition at check-in  
After checking in at the lobby after 4:00 PM, I entered my assigned room only to find a staff member inside repairing broken items. This was extremely surprising and uncomfortable, as I have never experienced such a situation in any hotel I have stayed at worldwide. A guest room should be fully prepared and inspected before being assigned to a guest.

2. Foreign object found during breakfast  
During breakfast, I discovered a hard, stone-like foreign object in the food. This raised serious concerns regarding food safety and hygiene and significantly affected my dining experience.

3. Inappropriate behavior by staff after check-out  
After checking out, I asked a staff member to help me get a taxi. When the staff asked for my destination, I answered in English. The staff member then sighed deeply in front of me, took my smartphone without permission, and checked the destination in Chinese. I found this behavior to be highly unprofessional and disrespectful.

That said, I would also like to acknowledge the positive aspects of my stay.  
I sincerely appreciated the room upgrade, the impressive and luxurious hotel facilities, and I thoroughly enjoyed my time at the casino, which was a memorable and enjoyable experience.

- HFO sent a follow up email to extend sincere apology, offered complimentary upgrade to premier suite for next visit.

- Case shared to relevant team for investigation and case study

rows.Incident Description:
SRC PD3B Ms. Fong Lai Wah, Tele booking cancelled for 23-24 Feb, 2026 in Conrad
(Ms. Fong stayed in Conrad on 19-20 Mar, 2026 in Rm#1702)

- Reported by Security team at 23:27hrs, one 82 years female guest fell down on L2 Link Bridge with bleeding on head. Security and EMT assisted to call ambulance then sent guest to Conde S. Januário Hospital in Macau.
rows.Subject: SRC PD3B Ms. Fong Lai Wah | Medical Assistance – 82 years female guest fell down on L2 Link Bridge
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Updated by Service Management :
Updated as of 16 Mar,  discharge form and bank details is received for insurance claims. 
Updated as of 3 Mar,  injured will have 3rd CT scan on 4 Mar and can be released from hospital if the condition allows. Communicated with GS Team tentative plan is to arrange one limo from LG to Conde S. Januário Hospital to Taipa Ferry Terminal on 5 Mar (date and time TBC). They will have one team member and wheelchair ready to accompany guest and her one family member all the way to Taipa Ferry Terminal. SM/Cindy will follow up with guest on the final CT result
Updated as of 2 Mar,  injured will take 3rd CT scan on 4 Mar,  so extended 3 Mar one night at casino rate,  4 Mar one night as hotel courtesy.
On 28 Feb,  SM/Cindy went to Conde S. Januário Hospital to visit the injured with Ms. Fong. Since she has diabetes and could only have the food provided by hospital,  we therefore brought a Chinese sweet soup to Ms. Fong as courtesy,  both the injured and Ms. Fong appreciated our seamless services very much and would definitely come back to us when the injured is fully recovered. 
Injured well beings is positive but still have very minor bleeding,  she is able to communicate,  eat and even go out of the ward with wheelchair sitted. They understood the case is just an accident and not showing obvious blames to hotel but would like to see if we can provide any claims for them (the medical bills around MOP 40, 000 so far),  SM/Cindy explained to guest we can assist on the claims but they must have the bills settled at hospital first. 
CT scan will be examined on 4 Mar and injured can be discharged form hospital if the bleeding is light. Ms. Fong planned to take CotaiJet to transfer the injured back to Hong Kong United Christian Hospital (Injured is elderly and have free healthcare in HK). SM/Cindy suggest we can offer limousine with wheelchair equipped to transfer the injured from Conde S. Januário Hospital to Taipa Ferry Terminal and the staff at CotaiJet can further assist to board her on the jet. 
Their family will take turns to take care the injured now:
1 Mar injured daughter Ms. Hui,  Shuk Man Brenda will stay with us one night to take care of injured ; Ms. Fong will go back to Hong Kong for work.
3 Mar Ms. Fong's son Hui Lok will stay with us to take care of injured.
SM/Cindy will follow up the case with above family members timely.

Updated by Service Management on 25-Feb:
25 Feb,  SM/Cindy contacted Ms. Fong to check on injured's condition,  Ms. Fong went to hospital last night and have two relatives accompanied but they will be back to Hong Kong later today. Injured remains conscious and the condition is improving. 2nd CT scan will be examined tomorrow for the next steps treatment. The ongoing treatment is blood transfusion,  control the bleeding,  given an antibiotic injection,  observe the blood pressure (blood pressure a bit high but it is in control after medication). Ms. Fong again thanked for our prompt action and concerns. We will constantly follow up this case after CT scan.

Updated by Service Management on 24-Feb:
At 10am,  Front Office give courtesy call to guest and learnt from guest that the injured required to stay in hospital for 2 weeks,  and she required extension of stay for 2 weeks and the medical claim follow-up.
At 11:30am,  Service Management (SM) has prepared lunch delivering to hospital for Ms. Fong. Before that extending courtesy call to Ms. Fong and learnt that Ms. Fong is on the way back to Londoner Grand (LG) for check in.
At 11:50am,  SM/Cindy meet Ms. Fong at LG main lobby after came back from hospital. She was visibly upset,  crying and emotional. She claimed that Mrs. Chan,  who is her husband’s mother,  is currently in a serious condition and needs to stay in the hospital for two weeks. Since other family members have to work in Hong Kong and cannot care for her in Macau,  Ms. Fong has no choice but to stay behind. She expressed deep concern about Ms. Chan’s condition and the subsequent medical expenses. SM/Cindy comforted Ms. Fong and explained the insurance claim procedure.
Ms. Fong recalled the day of the incident,  mentioning that she thought the travelator would go directly to The Londoner side instead of being divided into several segments. As a result,  she didn’t notice that this particular section had ended and therefore did not warn Ms. Chan. She did not place blame on our Company.
SM/Cindy has ordered lunch from In-Room Dining for Ms. Fong. She will take a rest in room and will visit hospital in evening. SM will continue to communicate with Ms. Fong through whatapps.

CCTV Footage reviewed:
At 231426hrs,  Female guest looked backward and did not aware that she arrived at the end of travellator #TN05.
(Ms. Chan was standing on the travelator with her back facing the direction of travel. Ms. Chan was turned towards Ms. Fong,  who was behind her to the right,  and had her left elbow resting on the handrail of the travelator.)
At 231428hrs,  she tripped by the travellator #TN05 then fell backward and hit the back of her head on the pillar. 
At 231443hrs,  HSKP TM passed by and approached to assist. 
At 231605hrs,  HSKP TM pressed the emergency button to stop the travellator#TN05.
At 231805hrs,  Security arrival.
rows.Investigation Remarks 2:
- Ms. Fong had one reservation of King Premier Suite in Conrad at 23-24 Feb with confirmation no. 3947110,  however had been cancelled at 22:29hrs on 23-Feb.
- The injured female guest Ms. Chan was family member of Ms. Fong.
- Ms. Fong requested a room for rest after back from hospital. Host relocated the booking to Londoner Grand since there was no room available at that moment in Conrad.
- CN HFO contacted LG HFO for further assistance with Ms. Fong. The room had been pre-checked in for guest already. Guests will be back to hotel at around 08:00-09:00hrs on 24-Feb.
- Updated legal platform INC1867.
- Case shared with Service Management team.
rows.Investigation Remarks 3:
Details of incident:
1. At 23:18hrs on 23-Feb,  Security called over the radio informing that a female guest (82-year-old,  No SRC) was injured at L2 Link Bridge Travellator #TN05 and requested to summon ambulance service. Security EMT responded to the location,  while SCR called for ambulance services. 
2. Surveillance footage review showed that at 23:14hrs,  the guest was facing the opposite side of the travellator,  and was not aware that she reached the end of travellator #TN05,  she then got tripped and fell backwards and hit her back head on the pillar. Meanwhile,  1 HSKP TM noticed the incident and pressed the emergency button to stop the travellator. 
3. At 23:29hrs,  ambulance arrived to B1 loading area and she was conveyed to the Macau CHCSJ Hospital accompanied by her female companion. No complaint was made. 
4. Injured female guest details: 
Ms. Chan Mei Lam who was 82 year (born in 1944) and held HKID

rows.Incident Description:
1. On 28 Feb 2026, at 15:17hrs, informed by Security, Ms. Wu's arm felt pain at Londoner Grand Lobby (she bumped it earlier in HK). EMT provided ice pack and recommended Ms. Wu to see the In-house Doctor or go to the nearby hospital for further medical checkup, however, she rejected. Ms. Wu claimed she wanted to see a doctor in Zhuhai and asked if hotel could assist her.
2. Service Assurance Manager (SAM) attended to the lobby immediately and learned that she had bumped her left arm in HK before, which caused the pain. She traveled along by ferry from HK today, upon arriving in Macao, she still felt pain. Considering the medical expenses in Macau are relatively high, she wanted to go to Zhuhai or return to HK for treatment. 
3. While talking with Ms. Wu, SAM learned that Ms. Wu has no family or friends in Zhuhai, but she has a domestic helper in HK who can accompany her and pick her at the HK-Macau Ferry Terminal. SAM suggested she return to HK for medical care. Ms. Wu agreed and asked for help canceling her reservation at Conrad and arranging a ferry ticket back to HK.
4. With Ms. Wu's consent, SAM accompanied her to the LG Sands Club counter and used her points to exchange for a free ferry ticket for the nearest available departure time (17:00hrs, Cotai Class, from Taipa Ferry Terminal to HK-Macau Ferry Terminal). Conard FOH also arrived at the counter and will assist Ms. Wu in her booking cancellation.
5. FOH and SAM accompanied Ms. Wu to the shuttle bus. The driver was informed about Ms. Wu's situation, Cotai Water Jet was also notified.
6. Since Ms. Wu was returning to HK alone, SAM added her on WhatsApp to follow up and make sure she arrived safely.
7. At 16:39hrs, informed by Cotai Water Jet that they had rescheduled Ms. Wu's ticket to 16:30hrs ferry, and she had successfully boarded.
8. At 17:55hrs, confirmed Ms. Wu was back to HK successfully via WhatsApp. Ms. Wu expressed her gratitude for the prompt service and concern.

rows.Incident Description:
At 16:20H, Mr. Zhong approached the GS counter, showed photos on his cellphone, and stated that our TM had damaged his cake. He added that the cake was custom-made in Zhuhai delivered to Macau by himself.
Investigation:
1.	At 1550H, Mr. Chong, a representative from an outside bakery, delivered a piece of cake to the GS counter at Crystal Palace, requesting it be sent to Conrad guest room 2622. As the cake was in an insulated bag, HGS1 asked Mr. Chong to take it out for a condition check. HGS1 inspected it and confirmed the cake was intact, after which Mr. Chong placed it back into the bag.
2.	At 16:05H, GRO1 delivered the cake to the guest in person. According to GRO1, he handed the cake to the guest at the door with both hands, and the guest received it with one hand. Since the cake was inside the bag, GRO1 could not verify its internal condition. 
3.	GSH1 submitted a request to the security for CCTV footage review, but no negative findings were identified.

Action taken:
1.	At 16:25H, HGS1 extended sincere apology to the guest in room 2622 for the unpleasant experience and offered to arrange a replacement cake from Churchill’s table, which the guest declined.
2.	At 18:20H HGS2 met Ms. Qi in the lobby and reiterated an apology for the inconvenience cased. learnt from Ms. Qi that after checking out the next day, they planned to take the 12:30H high-speed train from Zhuhai. To enhance their experience, a Londoner Taxi was arranged to take the guests to Qingmao Port at 11:10H, with luggage down service scheduled at 11:00H. Ms. Qi expressed her gratitude.  
3.	HGS2’s name card was handed to the guest for any further assistance needed.
4.	HGS will see off guest upon departure. Two Limited-edition Conrad bears and a box of Chocolate have been prepared as departure gift.
5.	This case will be shared and reviewed with the team to prevent similar incidents in the future.
6.	Guest emotional scale improved from 4 to 8.

rows.Incident Description:
LC#2882 Suspected Room Touting

- S#2882 under Mr. Zhao Zhili, PD1B SRC#4324521, stay period : 27Dec25 – 1Jan26.

- At 1900H, FOH was informed by BCC that a male guest, Mr. Li (only provide last name) called to Venetian PSC and transferred the call to BCC.
- Mr. Li requested a call back from manager regarding to room touting and he was going to Macao Police Station.
- Mr. Li provide a local phone number +853-6858-0340 to BCC.
- FOH called to Mr. Li with provided number and learnt detail from Mr. Li as below :
a. On 29Dec, Mr. Li watched Tiktok Live Stream and joined a “Room Selling” group chat.
b. Mr. Li would like to book a LC suite from the Tiktok channel. (Stay period : 31Dec25 – 3Jan26).
c. On 31Dec, Mr. Li met the male in Casino (did not disclose which casino) and the male sold the suite to Mr. Li with a cheaper price (6,000). Mr. Li didn’t disclose the currency and payment method.
d. At approximately 1530H/31Dec, Mr. Li claimed that he approached LC FO counter with the male guest.
e. The male guest get the room key at LC FO counter and passed to Mr. Li. Mr. Li claimed the card holder showed “A 2882”.
f. Mr. Li claimed he was informed the room was not clean yet. And, Mr. Li was requested to enter room later.
g. At approximately 1830H/31Dec, Mr. Li went up to S#2882 and found the key was not working.
h. Mr. Li heard sound from S#2882, then he rang the doorbell. A female guest opened the door from inside.
i. The female guest showed and told Mr. Li that she also paid the room from another booking source with 10,000 unknown currency.
j. Mr. Li then contacted the male in WeChat, who sold and passed the key to him. Mr. Li claimed the male blocked Mr. Li’s WeChat contact.
k. Mr. Li left hotel and waited his friend at MGM Cotai to pickup him to police station.
- FOH further asked if Mr. Li stored or put his personal belongings into S#2882.
- Mr. Li claimed he didn’t put any item into S#2882 and claimed he did not have item or money loss in S#2882.
- FOH politely informed hotel only have cooperation partner with Ctrip. And, no booking detail was disclosed to Mr. Li.
- Mr. Li showed understanding and did not peruse further, and he would look for police assistance.
- Case was shared to host and security manager.
- As of 0200H/01Jan26, no PSP or PJ contacted or approached hotel for the above case.

- Investigation as below :
a. There was no “guest card accepted” or “wrong key error” in S#2882 door log record during 1200H – 1900H on 31Dec25.
b. As per CCTV footage review, only HSKP entered S#2882 at 1746H and 1814H in the afternoon.
c. There are only 2 valid keys of S#2882, which was re-issue at 0900H on 31Dec25.
d. S#2882 had MUR request at 1000H. During MUR was being provided, guest was inside.
e. When HSKP provided S#2882 TDS at 1746H. No guest was inside.

Log was created for reference by FOH/Sam

Stay period: 3-7Jan

At 1732H on 6Jan, Mr. Cao from S#3063 reported a problem with the returned laundry and is requesting feedback.

FOH/Serena and HSKP HOD/Tommy attended to the suite and learned that three pieces of clothing were damaged. Two sweaters experienced shrinkage: a pink Fendi sweater, valued at MOP 6,000, and a white Moschino sweater, valued at MOP 2,000, both purchased on January 5 at the MGM shopping mall; the guest indicated they would provide the receipts the following day. Additionally, a coat valued at approximately RMB 4,000, which was purchased several months ago in South Korea, was also deformed, but no receipt was available for that item. Mr. Cao mentioned that when the HSKP TM collected the laundry, the guest specifically instructed to wash the items "according to the care label instructions."

Mr. Cao provided a photo of the pink Fendi sweater taken during the fitting, which shows visible shrinkage compared to the current item. 

FOH and HSKP HOD apologized to the guest and explained that it was necessary to contact and investigate the issue with the laundry company. Mr. Cao requested feedback by 1700H on January 7 to confirm compensation arrangements.

Host was informed above. Investigation by HSKP is pending.
rows.Subject: LO3063 | Mr. Cao Lei |Damage of laundry
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
At 1630H on 22jan,  Ms. Li called to FOH request for the compensation.

At 1635H,  FOH/Henry delivered Mop$3550 and waiver form to Ms. Li's suite (#1052,  registrant - Cao Lei,  Ms. Li husband). Ms. Li accepted the cash mop compensation and signed the waiver form. PM room number for F&B posting (Allowance - 5000Mop,  until 31Dec2026) has been informed to Ms. Li.

No further claims from Ms. Li.
rows.Investigation Remarks 2:
At 1700H,  FOH/Serena and HOD/Tommy visited Suite #3063,  where Ms. Li,  the wife of Mr. Cao,  was present. Explained the compensation matter related to the laundry company with her. According to the policy,  confirmed damages are compensated at ten times the laundry cost. 

According to the laundry list record,  compensation for Mrs. Cao's suit was determined to be 1, 750 MOP,  while the two sweaters were assessed at 2, 500 MOP. Mrs. Cao did not accept this offer. To address the inconvenience and negative experience,  FOH additionally offered a credit limit of 5, 000 MOP for use in food and beverage and spa services. After consideration,  Mrs. Cao accepted this offer. 

At 1900H,  Mrs. Cao called to clarify that two of the sweaters (Fendi and Moschino) belonged to her friend,  Ms. Yu (SRC# 6132363/PD2C). Ms. Yu stated that the sweaters were newly purchased and did not accept the ten-times-laundry-cost compensation. She also declined the F&B/SPA compensation option,  requesting instead to convert the 5, 000 MOP credit into shopping vouchers. Mrs. Cao noted that she would be leaving for Thailand the next day and would return to Macau in a couple of days. FOH added Mrs. Cao on WeChat and informed her that a response would be provided upon her return to Macau. 

Based on a receipt photo provided by the guest,  FOM contacted UMJ at One Central and confirmed that the items listed matched the actual items. The proposal suggests offering a shopping allowance of 5, 000 MOP,  which Ms. Yu can use to purchase clothing at The Londoner Shopping Centre. A cash refund will be provided upon submission of the receipt. If Smartable cannot provide cash compensation and the guest presents the original receipt,  the full amount will be compensated in MOP. All guests must sign the disclaimer form upon settlement.

Pending confirmation from Smartable regarding the compensation method by HSKP.

At 12:36H on 08 Jan,  FOH/Maika and EH/Frankie attended to the suite as Ms. Li already came back from Thailand and would like to follow up regarding the compensation. 

Ms. Li has been offered to have 5, 000 MOP hotel credits or a complimentary 1 night - Louis suite with 3, 000 MOP hotel credits,  in which she decided to accept the first offer of 5, 000 MOP hotel credits. Ms. Li was advised to communicate with FO,  should they prefer to consume the credits on their next visits and for restaurant or Spa reservations. Hotel credits are valid until the end of the year. 

During the conversation,  Ms. Li also mentioned about the compensation from the laundry company,  in which EH has politely explained that the procedure will take some time as it involves different department and proper protocol,  which Ms. Li understood. Housekeeping will follow up with Wardrobe/Linen and Smartable team accordingly. 

Furthermore,  Ms. Li requested to have the set of tweed green coat and skirt to send back to the laundry if they can remedy (stretch back to its normal size) and she will collect it on her next visit. Housekeeping will also follow up this matter with the Smartable. 

As Ms. Li just came back from Thailand,  a late check out until 14:00H was offered for her better rest.
rows.Investigation Remarks 3:
Investigation from Housekeeping:
- HSKP Linen Team received the guest's laundry on 3 January. Guest mentioned that would send it to wash according to the washing instructions on the label.

- Linen Team sent the clothing to Smartable according to guest requested,  when the laundry returned,  guest claimed 3 clothes were experienced shrinkage. (a pink Fendi sweater,  a white Moschino sweater and a Coat)

- Linen team already contacted Smartable for further follow-up,  pending reply tomorrow.

- S#2390 under Mr. Zhu Hongxun, PD2B SRC#6073207, stay period : 06-09Jan26.
- At 0450H, a female guest called to BCC and requested the Iodine swabs for Mr. Zhu because he slipped and fell in the bathroom and his calves was hurt.

A. Mr. Lin slipped and fell backwards in the bathroom after he came out from the shower room. Mr. Lin didn't mention if he wears the slipper.
B. His both calves was abraded by the bottom edge of vanity counter and hit his left rear head at the wall of shower room. (refers to attachment)
C. There was a minor abrasion on both calves and there was no wound on his left rear head. (refers to attachment)

- FOH further offered in-house doctor and suggested Mr. Lin to have checkup at hospital, but Mr. Lin rejected.

-	At 2104H, FOH was informed by BCC that #2594 Mr. Chen Ersheng requested assistance as 5yrs old boy (Chen Zhiquan 陈志权, DOB: 20210115; CF6118131) accidently slip and fall in bathroom and hurt the chin. BCC had contacted EMT; and informed HSKP to deliver one extra non-slip mat.
-	At 2109H, FOH, EMT and Security manager rushed to room. The boy was lying on sofa with bathrobe. Learnt from Mr. Chen that the boy is taking bath in master bedroom bathtub. He planned to stand up by holding the bathtub pillow; however, the pillow is not stable and suddenly dropped down, which caused the boy lost balance and fell down; the chin hit on the bathtub and got about 3cm wound with bleeding. Mr. Chen suspected the aging of the bathtub pillow had caused it to become unstable. FOH extended empathy for the case happed and offered to replace a new bathtub pillow; which was declined by Mr. Chen. Guest declined TM to touch anything around the bathtub.
-	EMT assisted with disinfection with bandage. Mr. Chen asked if the wound can be recovered by itself; TM suggested guest to go hospital for further check as the wound consider quite deep (guest rejected TM to take photo). Meanwhile Mrs. Chen came back with a girl from Concert. After discussion with Mr. Chen, guest decided to go hospital for further check.
-	Mr. Chen asked FOH how to settle the medical fee. FOH kindly informed guest to pay the bill first and pass the receipt to hotel; hotel would forward to Risk Management for further follow up.
-	Mr. Chen got emotional and claimed hotel should pay for all medical bills directly as the case happened in hotel. FOH extended apology for the inconvenience. 
-	After further confirmed with higher management and Risk management, guest had to settle medical fee in hospital first then hotel assisted to apply for further follow up.
-	To void further delay on the injured boy, FOH escorted Mrs. Chen and the boy to get on limo heading to Macau Union Hospital with Butler accompany. 
-	FOH got in touch with host. After further discussion, host would like to comp the medical fee. After got further approval from management, FO paid out cash and arranged TM to deliver it to hospital.
-	At 2352H, FOH met with Mrs. Chen and the boy at LG by return limo. Learnt from Mrs. Chen that doctor applied 3 stitches; and need go the designated health authority to change the dressing on 11Jan day time. FOH advised Mrs. Chen to contact FO for limo booking at any time. Kids puzzles and a Portuguese-style Barcelos Rooster were passed to the boy as a gesture of goodwill. Mrs. Chen further mentioned that they always use the bathtub pillow on previous stay; however, this is the 1st time to encounter it unstable. Medical bill $1178 original was passed to Finance; and all document copy was passed to Mrs. Chen.
-	FOH escorted guests back to #2594 and extended courtesy to Mr. Chen, while guest was drinking. Pata Nagra and fresh platter were delivered to Mr. Chen for wine pairing. 
- Mr. Chen insisted to file the case to Police as 1) the boy slip and fall due to the unstable pillow; 2) hotel informed guest to pay medical bill first in hospital.
-	FOH tried to calm down guest however guest insisted to call Police as soon as possible. FOH excused herself and made call to Security shift manager for further assistance.
-	To void disturbance Mr. Chen opened door from inside again and noted the children are about to resting, at 0004H, FOH kept the door latch on and waited for Security in L25 D lift lobby. Security Supervisor arrived L25 D zone lift lobby at 0010H.  When FOH and Security had conversation in lift lobby at 0013H, Mr. Chen came out and asking why the door is not fully closed. FOH extended apology immediately, Mr. Chen took out phone and took 3 videos of FOH and two security TMs; informed he would post the video to social media. Mr. Chen closed the door at 0018H.
-	Around 0057H, PSP attended to room with Security, FOH. PSP confirmed with Mr. Chen that no items were missing during the door latch on period. PSP verbally informed Mr. Chen that it is not permitted to film or publish other’s video to social media without the individual’s consent. 
-Mr. Chen further claimed that he would hire a lawyer to sue the hotel.
-	PSP continued to gather more information from Mr. Chen on the boy’s injury. One more PSP arrived #2594 afterwards. Mr. Chen insisted PSP to take away the bathtub pillow as exhibit; and insisted to file the case as a criminal case rather than a civil one, as the boy was injured; which was turn down by PSP; and PSP advised guest to contact MGTO on this request. 
-	At 0231H, Mr. Chen asked two PSP and TMs left #2594.
-	Log was forward to Risk management; legal platform #1799 was updated. The case CVML3710 had been reported to our insurance company for record.
-	Pending to update host on 11Jan.
-	Pending FO to extend courtesy and arrange limo on 11Jan.

rows.Incident Description:
Room 3456/ C#4198400
Booking Source: FIT, Ctrip
Name: Ms. Wang Qingyun& Ms. Du Yinglei
Stay period: 14-16Jan


At 2354H on 15Jan, Ms. Wang, from S#3456, reached out to GR through WeChat to express her dissatisfaction regarding the tidying of her bed, despite her request for it to remain untouched. The GR team inquired about her availability for a phone call, to which Ms. Wang responded that she would get in touch after freshening up. At 0052H on 16Jan, she confirmed her willingness to meet, prompting the FOH/Serena and HOD to proceed to her room immediately.

Ms. Wang stated that during check-in the previous night, she had notified housekeeping not to disturb her belongings due to her cleanliness preferences. She mentioned using her own disposable bedding and had asked for ten extra towels to cover the sofa, chairs, and carpet and appeared frustrated during the conversation. FOH apologized and suggested disinfecting the room and changing the bedding immediately, but Ms. Wang declined, as she had already placed her own disposable sheets. She requested only two additional fresh towels.

During the discussion, Ms. Wang expressed her dissatisfaction with her stay, noting that she had booked a twin-bed room but received a king bed instead. FOH explained that the reservation indicated a king bed, which may have resulted from incomplete information from the third-party booking platform (Booking source: Ctrip). She also mentioned that her tight schedule prevented her from enjoying the hotel’s afternoon tea and cocktail offerings. FOH then offered complimentary white wine and a cheese platter to help her relax, which she declined. Ms. Wang subsequently requested breakfast for four at The Residence for the following day. FOH politely declined but offered a MOP 1,000 dining credit instead. She then requested to arrange breakfast for six-seven at The Churchill’s Table at 1200H on 16Jan, FOH reminded the guest that this is the peak dining period and breakfast service ends at 1300H. To ensure a pleasant dining experience, FOH suggested North Palace as an alternative. Ms. Wang acknowledged this but continued to express her preference for The Churchill's Table.

Ms. Wang shared her gratitude for the room attendant who assisted her the previous night, noting their patience. She also appreciated our response to her concerns and mentioned that she would choose our hotel for her next business trip. FOH thanked her for the feedback and assured her that the team would take extra care to personalize her experience during future visits.

GR team will greet guests during breakfast.

Investigation by FO:

Ms. Wang checked in at 2350H on 14Jan, while checking in and confirming the reservation details, Ms. Wang stated that they had booked a twin-bed room and asked if the room had been deep-cleaned as requested. GRO confirmed that the room had been prepared accordingly and offered to arrange a room change, which Ms. Wang declined. 

Other pending investigation by HSKP.

6. Ms. Huang and Ms. Zhang decided to change to stay at Londoner Court.

9. When Ms. Huang and Ms. Zhang arrived LC LG Lobby, GS TM A picked all the luggage from Ms. Huang (Suitcase, brown handbag and the white tote bag) and escorted them to LG lift lobby.

11. After guest checked in, GS TM B escorted guests from lobby to S#3483. Ms. Huang and Ms. Zhang was walking around inside the living room while GS TM B carried the luggage into the dressing room.

13. After GS TM B left S#3483, Ms. Huang didn’t do the money count immediately. And, she took a picture of her luggage inside the dressing room (refers to the attachment).
14. Ms. Huang relocated her brown handbag (refers to the attachment) to another closet. And she took out her personal items from the suitcase.
15. Ms. Huang and Ms. Zhang rested inside S#3483 and woke up at approximately 1900H.

rows.Incident Description:
1.At approximately 00:08 at night, informed by FO GRO that an elderly person and a 3-year-old child in Room 1693 had slipped and fallen in the bathtub, they just passed by the FO counter, heading to LG and request to clean the guest bathroom of 1693.

2.FOH immediately went to the LG where the guests (the elderly, the child, Mr. Shi and his wife) had already on the taxi and were rushing to Union Hospital for emergency treatment. FOH intended to ask about the incident details but failed to do so due to the guests' urgent need for medical treatment. Meanwhile, FOH immediately reported the incident to the Host.

3.Mr. Shi requested to clean the guest bathroom of Room 1693 due to a large amount of blood had been left at the scene where his father-in-law fell.

4.FOH then went to Room 1693 and confirmed a large amount of blood in the guest bathroom, with no blood or abnormalities found in the master bathroom.

5. The 12-year-old elder son of Mr. Shi was in the room and confirmed that there were 5 occupants in total: Mr. and Mrs. Shi, their 12-year-old elder son, 3-year-old youngest son, and the 64-year-old elderly male. (Mr. Shi’s father-in-law-Mr. Meng)

6.FOH immediately informed HSKP to fully clean the bloodstains in the guest bathroom.

7. The guest party returned to Room 1693 from Union Hospital at approximately 02:37, and FOH went to the room at 02:50 to express concern and to learn about the details of the slip and fall.

8. Since the Shi family was about to rest, Mr. Shi only briefly described the incident: while the Mrs. Shi was bathing the two children, the 3-year-old youngest son slipped and fell while frolicking and jumping in the bathroom, suffering an approximately 3-centimeter laceration on his chin; Mr. Meng was taking a bath in the guest bathroom, and when he heard the child crying, he got up to check on the child, accidentally slipped and fell out of the bathtub, sustaining nasal injuries and an approximately 4-5 centimeter laceration on his left supraorbital ridge.
9. Mr. Shi informed that after the preliminary diagnosis and treatment by the doctor, the elderly male received sutures for the laceration on his supraorbital ridge, while the 3-year-old child's chin laceration was only bandaged without suturing. Due to the severe injuries, Mr. Meng was temporarily kept under observation and treatment in Union Hospital; as the hospital did not have the corresponding clinical department, Mr. Shi planned to discuss whether to transfer Mr. Meng to a hospital in Zhuhai or other places for further treatment the next morning.

10. Mr. Shi also stated that the family originally planned to return to Shanghai the next day, but the trip might be delayed due to the incident, and the subsequent travel arrangements would be determined based on the recovery of Mr. Meng and the child's conditions.

11. Mr. Shi informed the FOH that they did not need any assistance from the hotel for the time being, and would contact the hotel after the family got up the on next day if necessary.

12. The host confirmed that Mr. Shi was a friend of main guest Mr. Lyu and Mr.Lyu indicated that Mr. Shi could handle the incident on his own.

13.Pending FOH to extend courtesy on the next day.

14.Case has been uploaded to the incident platform.

rows.Incident Description:
Room 1255| C#4240807
SRC# 2810821| PD3B
Name: Mr. Ye, Xiaolong
Stay period: 6-9Feb	

At 2030H on 7 February, the limousine manager, Terrence, arrived at the front desk and requested to visit the guest Mr. Ye, who was staying in Suite #1255. 

Terrence explained that the drivers were transporting Mr. Ye and his family from the airport to the hotel at midnight on 7 Feb when a sudden brake caused a child in the vehicle to injure her lip, resulting in bleeding. Terrence wished to visit the guest to express concern and inquire about the child’s current condition.

FOS Charles promptly called Suite #1255 to obtain Mr. Ye’s consent and then accompanied Terrence to the suite.
 
Terrence inquired about the child’s injury, which Mr. Ye replied that the child was now fine (Daughter is 6 yrs old. No further information is disclosed). However, Mr. Ye expressed strong dissatisfaction with the driver.
. Noting that the vehicle did not slowdown in advance when approaching a turn and only reduced speed after Mr. Ye had reminded the driver. This was followed by the sudden brake that led to the child's injury. 
. After the incident, the driver took the family to a clinic, which was closed. Mr. Ye ultimately took a taxi on his own to Union Hospital for treatment. 

Terrence and FOS both expressed their apologies for the incident and proposed to file an insurance claim for the child, as well as to arrange limousine for their departure. However, Mr. Ye declined their offers, stating that he had already arranged a limousine for his departure on 8Feb and emphasized his expectation for accountability regarding the driver's actions.

Investigation from Front Office:
 -S#1255 was prechecked in at 2345H on February 6, upon the host's request. 
-Mr. Ye checked in at 0240H on 7Feb. During the check-in process, Mr. Ye did not report any incident, and the front desk staff did not observe that a child was accompanying him. 
-After reviewing the limousine system, it was noted that Mr. Ye had scheduled a limousine from LPC to MIA at 0730H on 8Feb. FOH will prepare a bag of CT amenities, which includes two shortbread cookies and one ginger tea, and will see off Mr. Ye and his family on 8Feb.

Other items are still under investigation by the Limousine Service Team.

Guest name: Ms. Lu Fen/ Mr. Yang Yunhai
Stay Period: 10-13Feb2026
Booking Source: FIT / Sands direct booking
Room number: Windsor suite S#1452, party with S#1460 and S#1461. 

1.	At 1900H on 12Feb, Ms. Lu and her family approached The Residence for evening cocktail and reported to GRO that the power socket in her room had damaged her phone, therefore, she bought a new phone at the Londoner Apple store.
2.	GRH apologized to Ms. Lu, Ms. Lu stated that her iPhone 17Pro malfunctioned after being charged with an Apple charging cable via the USB socket in the living room of S#1452, caused the mainboard of her iPhone 17Pro to break down and could not be turned on.
3.	Ms. Lu further mentioned she had used the same socket and charging cable two days earlier, but the function was normal, suspected the power socket malfunction suddenly.  
4.	Ms. Lu went to the Apple Store at Londoner for consultation, since she had purchased her iPhone 17 Pro with AppleCare+ in mainland China, Apple store in Macao is only providing the basic hardware inspection and paid repair service, so she bought a new iPhone 17 Pro as an emergency replacement because she planned to stay in Macao for another three nights at Four Seasons Hotel on 13-16Feb.
5.	GRH extended the sincere apology for the inconvenience caused and contacted FAC and HSKP HOD to conduct a thorough inspection of the power socket in S#1452, which guest accepted and agreed to be present during the inspection. 
6.	FAC MOD found that all USB sockets were operating under normal voltage (2A) in the living room of S#1452, while the phone charging cable was rated at 6A and all functions was normal.
7.	FAC MOD also tested the charging function of his own phone using the same power socket and same charging cable, all functions remained normal. 
8.	GRH kindly explained to Ms. Lu, she showed her understanding and accepted the explanation. 
9.	Learnt from Ms. Lu that they would check in at Four Seasons Hotel on 13Feb, late check out at 3pm and luggage service had been arranged. Further found out that Ms. Lu and her family planned to visit Macao Peninsula for sightseeing over the next two day, around trip limousine had been arranged as hotel courtesy. 
10.	Ms. Lu appreciated that and without further requests. 

Investigation: 
1.	6A charging cable will only draw the maximum current the power socket can supply (2A), resulting in slower charging, but it will not damage the charger or device.
2.	All power sockets are under normal conditions in the living room.
3.	Didn’t receive any previous feedbacks from guests about damaged phones caused by the power socket in the room at Londoner hotel.

Legal platform was updated with INC1853.

1.	At 1925H on 15Feb, Mr. Wang and his family approached ML for check in.
2.	GR SUP informed guest that total amount of MOP85000 for both rooms (Room charge MOP79331.6 and incident deposit MOP5000)
3.	However, Mr. Wang claimed that the room charge should be total MOP68984 net on booking.com (please refer to the attachment).
4.	GR SUP explained and confirmed the room rate again in Opera, but Mr. Wang refused to pay the actual room charge in Opera. 
5.	GR SUP explained to guest that will further follow up with Travel Agency and Mr. Wang agreed to pay deposit of MOP75000 (Room charge MOP68984 and incident deposit MOP5000).
6.	GR team confirmed the room rate with Travel Agency and tried to explain to Mr. Wang via WeChat, but Mr. Wang didn’t reply to the message. 
7.	GR SUP met Mr. Wang at The Residence during breakfast on 18Feb, GR SUP kindly explained the room rate difference issue to Mr. Wang, but he got upset.
8.	GR HEAD contacted to Travel Agency on 18Feb, Travel Agency claimed they failed to contact Mr. Wang by phone call and insisted hotel to charge him MOP79331.6.
9.	Since Booking.com and Mr. Wang had not yet reached an agreement, GRH explained to Mr. Wang that the room charge would be charged to his credit card upon check- out tomorrow according to the rate in Opera (MOP79331.6).
10.	Mr. Wang was advised to contact Booking.com directly afterwards to apply for any refund or compensation for the room rate difference.

Investigation: 
1.	Booking was created on 16Jan2026, stay period is 15-19Feb2026. The room rate is MOP 40240.8 for Victoria suite and MOP 39090.8 for Louis suite, total MOP 79331.6 in Opera.
2.	Since Mr. Wang booked the room in CNY via Booking.com, the currency displayed was CNY 59207.71 + additional taxes and service fees CNY 8881, which converts to MOP 68984.
3.	However, this amount did not include taxes and service fees in the display on Booking.com platform, which caused misunderstanding for Mr. Wang. 

Follow up: 
1.	GR Team will follow up with Booking.com before Mr. Wang check out tomorrow to get a response or agreement, so as to avoid charging Mr. Wang’s credit card without his permission.
2.	Courtesy offered complimentary departure limousine from Londoner Hotel to Grand Lisboa Palace at 1400H on 19Feb by Londoner Taxi, CNY gift boxes will be prepared as farewell gift due to high-rate FIT guests.

However,  the hotel is willing to offer her a complimentary room upgrade for her next stay as a gesture of goodwill. rows.Incident Description:
Incident Report
 
Date: March 5, 2026
Guest: Ms. Liu, Golden Sands Membership Card No: 151983|RM21402
 
Event Details
 
1. At around 5:00 AM on March 5, Ms. Lau dined at the Chelsea Garden restaurant and enjoyed 2 set meals. The staff processed and redeemed the SRC set menu vouchers as per standard procedure.
2. In the afternoon of March 5, Ms. Lau returned to the restaurant, claiming that 2 vouchers were missing. It was confirmed that the 2 vouchers had expired.
3. The vouchers were issued on February 28 with a 3-day validity period, expiring on March 4. They were already invalid at 12:00am on March 5.  Duty lead Wendy explained the validity policy to the guest, but she became very upset and questioned the staff loudly before leaving.
4. At 9:00 PM, the guest called the restaurant via the front office to complain again. Staff explained that the voucher expiry date was clearly shown in the app, and the vouchers expired after midnight on March 4.
5. The guest remained extremely angry and complained continuously for nearly 30 minutes, demanding the issue be escalated to Golden Sands Membership for a resolution.
6. Duty lead Alan escalated the case to SRC, The feedback received was that all vouchers clearly state the validity period; no compensation will be provided in accordance with company policy.
 
Outcome & Follow-up
 
- The restaurant has explained the voucher validity policy to the guest multiple times and followed proper procedures throughout.
- The case has been escalated and officially reviewed by SRC, No compensation or special arrangement is approved.
- If the guest returns, maintain a consistent and polite explanation, avoid conflicts, and escalate to a supervisor or membership team if necessary.
rows.Subject: Chelsea Garden | Ka Hang  Lau | High Demanding Guest Asking Refund SRC Set Menu Voucher

rows.Incident Description:
A visitor, Mr. Chen Lian Shen, complained his son was hit on the head with a phone by someone at the Taxi Stand. 
	At about 1940hrs, GSH was informed by the Taxi Stand TM that a departing guest complained someone hit his son’s head by phone at Taxi Stand and requested to check CCTV. 
	As per the Taxi Stand TM, he called the standby Police Officer to assist the male guest after a brief communication with Mr. Chen, because the standby security officer went to handle a car incident. Only Mr. Chen left at the Taxi Stand to wait for the result. 
	While waiting for the result from CCTV, GSH, Security Supervisor Ken and one police officer attended Mr. Chen at the Taxi Stand. Mr. Chen was calm but kept saying two issues: 1. Must have someone hit his son’s head by phone, otherwise, his son will not cry hardly; 2. The TM standby at the Taxi Stand did not show enough care to them. 
	GSH apologized for Mr. Chen for the incident and asked if his son needed medical attention; however, Mr. Chen declined and stated that there was no need. GSH asked Mr. Chen to exchange the contact for following up the incident, Mr. Chen declined too. 
	At about 2010hrs, another Security Supervisor Branda approached Mr. Chen and stated that it was too blur to confirm how his son was hurt, because limited CCTV coverage and also many people were waiting for taxi at that moment. Mr. Chen was not completely satisfied with the result and kept saying the Bell standby the Taxi Stand was not helpful enough and will complain this if he comes to stay in the future. And then Mr. Chen left by taxi. 
	As per the police officer’s request, Mr. Chen left his contact details to the Security Team. 
	At about 20:42, Security Supervisor Branda called GSH Head and shared that they found new clues through another camera at driveway and already informed Mr. Chen and Mr. Chen expressed appreciation to their assistance. And the new clue is Mr. Chen went to the queue through the taxi side of the Taxi Stand and his son tried to catch up in the behind and crossed the guest who was just trying to enter the taxi, there was contact of the guest’s hand and the kid’s head. 
	As per the TM standby the Taxi Stand, Mr. Chen talked to him loudly to request to check the CCTV. And he only asked where the kid was hit and Mr. Chen became irritate immediately. 
	Guest emotion scale is about 7 after learning the newest update from the Security team and did need any follow up. 
	GS team will share more how to engage with guest in emergency situations during briefing. Security reference number 26045-0842.
-  As per Mr. Chen, the kid is 9 years old.

Incident Details:

At 23:47 on 18Apr, informed by GS Supervisor as below:

1.	At 22:54, Mr. Wang approached FO and asked why his luggage was not yet delivered to his room #1381 and he had requested long time ago. FO apologized to Mr. Wang and contacted GS Supervisor immediately.

1.	At 21:48 on 18Apr, Mr. Wang passed a Londoner Luggage Tag to FO and requested to fetch his luggage (one piece of suitcase) to his room #1381. FO dispatched the job via FCS system accordingly.
2.	GS GRO proceeded to Londoner GS and got the suitcase from there. However, at 22:04, the GS GRO delivered to room #3181 instead of #1381.
3.	At 22:51, Mr. Wang left his room and approached FO as he still not received the suitcase yet.
4.	At 23:07, Mr. Wang’s suitcase was delivered back to his room #1381.
5.	It took 1 hour and 19 minutes from Mr. Wang’s request was received to the job was done. (21:48-23:07).
6.	Mr. Wang had not returned to his room yet for the whole night.

Follow Up:
The case has been shared among the whole GS team and emphasize it’s a must to double confirm the room number. GS will extend apologies in person and follow up with service recovery.

rows.Incident Description:
1. On 22 Apr 2026, at 17:15H, informed by SEC, a female guest, who was later identified as LC Suite#3086 Mr. Chan's friend, Ms. Wang (D.O.B. 1969/Mar), was injured at the PG entrance shuttle bus waiting area.
2. SAM and EMT arrived at the scene, The registered guest Mr. Chan was also on the scene. Learnt from Ms. Wang that, at around 17:00H, while she was at the Border Gate about to board the shuttle bus to The Londoner, she tripped and fell forward onto the ground due to uneven pavement at that area. Observed that Ms. Wang had bleeding wounds on both knees and her right elbow. EMT was ready to provide first aid immediately, but Ms. Wang said that since there were many people in the lobby, she preferred to have first aid in the room. After checking the wounds (no heavy bleeding, and because Ms. Wang was wearing long sleeves and long pants when she fell, the wounds had no direct contact with the ground and there was no dirt or sand), EMT agreed to do the first aid after going back to room. SAM assisted with the luggage, EMT pushed Ms. Wang in a wheelchair, along with one Shuttle Services Supervisor, escorted guests returned to the room together. LC FOH was informed.
3. After returning to the room, EMT provided first aid, and extra ice packs and band-aids were offered. Since Ms. Wang mentioned that she still felt some pain when walking, SAM suggested that she rest and monitor for a few, if she needed to go hospital, she could contact us at any time, and we would arrange limo for her. SAM offered laundry service for Ms. Wang due to her clothes were soiled when she fell. Ms. Wang expressed her gratitude but declined.
4. Upon learning that guest planned to go to Hip Seng Hot Pot for dinner later, FOH provided a wheelchair for the room.
5. SAM will contact Shuttle Service for the on-site pictures of the accident area to assess the risk and discuss with relevant departments whether improvements can be made.
6. Legal Platform: INC1952

1.At around 00:35, it was reported by the Butler that Mr. Sun and his friend were checking into an occupied room.

1. Mr. Du xuefei(#SRC 6369269 PD1A) held two reservations under his name, Room 3490 and Room 2181. At 13:23 on the 25th, the host sent an email to request a shorten stay for Room 3490, followed by another email at 13:25 stating “Ignore please”. Shortly after, the host issued another email to apply the shorten stay to Room 2181 instead. It is suspected that the main cause of this incident was the FO TM failing to notice the “Ignore please” remark from the host, resulting in incorrect processing of shorten stay and check-out for Room 3490.

After Housekeeping updated the room status to VI at 16:00, the original guests returned to Room 3490 at 18:04 and continued their stay with their valid keys.
3. FOH also confirmed that Room 3490 was occupied by Mr. Du Xuefei’s friends, who were having supper at that time. The FOH personally visited the room to extend a sincere apology. Two mango sago were prepared to the guests as dessert after their meal. The guests did not take the matter further and thanked for the assistance.

rows.Incident Description:
Guest Name: Ms. Hu Yizhi
Stay Period: 28-30Apr26
Room number: 2965
Booking Source: FIT / Ctrip

-	At 1651H on 29Apr, received WeChat call from Ms. Wu, she stated that she was outside room 2965 and unable to open the door with her room key.  
-	GR SUP contacted HSKP floor SUP for immediate assistance. Minutes after, GR HEAD received a call from TA- Ctrip, mentioned Ms. Wu had lodged a complaint regarding the malfunctioning room key and the lack of immediate assistance to open the door. 
-	GR HEAD attended to 29F and met Ms. Wu together with her husband while Ms. Wu was opening the door from inside room 2965.     
-	Ms. Wu was highly agitated and upset, and raised the following complaints:
1.	Room key malfunction: Ms. Wu claimed her room key suddenly failed to open the room door for unknown reason, caused her locked outside the room with her husband and two kids. 
2.	Delayed & Unsuccessful assistance: Ms. Wu’s husband requested assistance from HSKP RA to open the door, but the issue remained unsolved for around 20 minutes waiting as he was not the registration guest. Eventually, she opened the room door with the room key successfully. 
3.	Suspected insect bite inside the room: Ms. Wu had multiple red lumps on her legs, which she believed were caused by insect in the room as she mentioned had not left the hotel for the past two days.

-	GR HEAD expressed sincere concern and apology to guest, but Ms. Wu kept shouting in 29F corridor.
-	GR HEAD escorted Ms. Wu to The Residence for afternoon tea and offered compensation, including late check out and Londoner Taxi as departure limousine. Afterwards, Ms. Wu began to claim down.
-	GR HEAD offered room move and medical assistance but Ms. Wu declined. After a brief on-site check inspection by HSKP SUP and GR HEAD, no mosquitoes or inserts were found inside 2965. All linen was replaced with hypoallergenic items, and the welcome fruit and desserts were removed from the room. 


Investigation:
1. System and door lock records showed both room keys were valid and successfully unlocked the door at 1644H and 1652H. Suspected guest didn’t open the door immediately after unlocked the door by room key.   

2. HSKP RA accompanied Ms. Wu’s husband to call PSC via the public telephone on 29F. PSC could not verify his identify as he was not registered in Opera, Ms. Wu’s husband explained Ms. Wu was outside the room with two kids and unable to answer the phone. PSC advised HSKP RA to bring the husband to meet registration guest Ms. Wu and call PSC again via duty phone for identity verification. However, PSC didn’t receive any further follow- up calls. 

HSKP SUP rushed to 29F after received a call from GR, but guest had already opened the door with their room key.  

Ms. Wu approached FO counter alone for check in on 28Apr, hence her husband was not registered in the system.    

3. No mosquitoes or inserts were found during the room inspection, her family did not have any insect bite marks. HSKP will follow up after guest checked out on 30Apr.

Follow up:
-	GR team will show concern to guest during breakfast on 30Apr. 
-	Guest’s profile was updated for hypoallergenic linen set up.

rows.Incident Description:
Guest Name: Mr. Chen Yun Yu/Mr. Chung Pei Ling
Stay Period: 13 – 16 Jan 2026
Room Number/Type: KC > QF(22105)
Booking Source: FIT Booking (Agoda)
Nationality: TW


1.	At 13:30hrs, GS SUP/Queenie received a report from GS GRO that Mr. Chen, a passenger who disembarked from the Macau International Airport shuttle bus, discovered his luggage was missing from the bus, but a 26-inch suitcase of the exact same color was found on the bus, but not own by them. Said luggage sent to security. The bus route airport-Londoner-Parisian.

2.	GS Sup/Queenie assisted in contacting other hotel properties: The Londoner/St. Regis/LG/Conrad, and Londoner L&F. There were no reports of lost luggage at that time, but the FO reception and GS teams were advised to keep records so that they could inform any guests who approached the counter inquiring about the situation.

3.	At 13:40hrs, during the conversation with the guests, GS Sup/Queenie learned that Mr. and Mrs. Chen had come to the Parisian Hotel with their child to celebrate a birthday. GS Sup led the guests to the FO reception desk and informed FO GRO about the lost luggage. Since the guests had a child with them and were here to celebrate a birthday, FO GRO assisted the guests with immediate check-in and free upgraded them from KC to QF. GS Sup then escorted the guests and their family back to room 22105.

4.	CSH/Dilly notified the SEC team to review CCTV footage of the disembarkation areas outside the Londoner and Parisian driveways to see if any passengers had mistakenly taken similar luggage during that time. CSH also contacted the Macau International Airport L&F to inquire about the contact information of the passengers who had mistakenly taken luggage and to ask if any other passengers had reported similar cases.

5.	Since the guest is from Taiwan, we were unable to contact them. However, the airport L&F informed us that due to security concerns, they could not provide contact information. They have tried adding the guest on WeChat and WhatsApp and are waiting for their reply.

6.	At 17:30hrs, CSH/Dilly called to Room# 22105 Mr. Chen, and inform the guest about the luggage search and suggest that they report it to the police, which may help find the luggage more quickly. CSH will assist guest together to report to police to help speed up the locating of luggage.

7.	At 17:40hrs, CSH was waiting for Mr. Chen in the lobby, two Taiwanese guests approached with what appeared to be a pink 26-inch suitcase. They had mistakenly taken the wrong suitcase when they got off at the Londoner Hotel. Mr. Chen arrived at the lobby just then and confirmed the suitcase belonged to him. With the presence of the PC PSP and security personnel, it was confirmed that the suitcase was locked and nothing was missing; they had simply taken the wrong Mr. Chen's luggage. rows.Incident Description:
1.	On 21 Jan, Guest feedback was received via Ctrip claiming R#16076 experienced a sudden power outage lasting 2-3 mins at 0042H on 20Jan while Ms. Li was showering.  
2.	FOH/Leanne contact Facility MOD/Felix to relay the guest’s comments and inquire whether any power issued had been recorded from R#16076 in recent days. 
3.	As confirmed by Facility that 2-3 mins power off was likely due to a sensor failure to detect guest movement, resulting in the room remaining in power-saving mode
4.	FOH/Leanne made courtesy call to Ms. Li to obtained more details of the case. 
5.	During phone conversation, Ms. Li recalled that while she was showering and her child was sleeping, the power went out. She mentioned that while moving cautiously from the bathtub toward the living room in the dark, she hit her nose, causing it to bleed. She stated she still feels unwell. 
6.	FOH expressed sympathy and advise Ms. Li that she can visit hospital if necessary, assuring her that the hotel would assist with medical reimbursement through the risk management process after case investigation.
7.	Leanne politely explained to Ms. Li that the room is set energy-saving mode as part of the hotel’s ECO-Friendly of the design and offered a courtesy ( F&B Voucher$300/ QUBE Access/ 2 x pax Breakfast / Future suite upgrade)  as gesture of goodwill. Ms. Li decline all offers and instead requested a full room charge refund or direct cash compensation. 
8.	FOH/Leanne polity decline on room charge/cash refund compensation request and kindly reminded the guest to contact front office for further medical assistance. 
9.	After check review guest stay records, shows that Ms. Li did not report any power issue during her stay, which ended on 20 Jan. The feedback was submitted to C-Trip on 21 Jan. 
10.	The incident log has been shared with the facility team for further investigation
        
Log Created by FOH/Leanne
rows.Subject: PA - 716076 | Ms. Chen Li | Guest Feedback room has 2-3 mins power off
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Housekeeping update on 22-Jan:
Today (January 22nd),  Facility team checked the room's lighting system and found it to be working properly. The cause of this incident is that the sensor in the room is located next to the bed. It is estimated that after the guest entered the room,  she did not pass the sensor and went directly into the bathroom. The timer expired without detecting the presence of a guest in the room,  so the lighting system entered energy-saving mode.

Log update by HSKP EH Eric

Investigation Details:

1. The previous guest of R #14038, Mr. Shao Guangqiang (PD2C#3199134), checked in on 19 February at the Plaza Loft. Mr. Shao had back-to-back reservations until 23 February.
2. Upon verification with PL/GRO, Mr. Shao was fully informed that his stay was until 23 February, and a key valid through 23 February was issued via Visionline accordingly.
3. On 21 February at approximately 14:53, Mr. Shao approached Front Office Supervisor#65280, claiming he had a suite booking on 21 Feb and that Room #14038 had been checked out.

5. A new key for Suite #22068 was issued by Supervisor #65280 to Mr. Shao; however, she failed to deactivate the key for Room #14038.
6. According to the door lock system, the last housekeeping team entered R#14038 at 17:21 to inspect the room, and the room status was released as "Vacant Inspected" at 17:22.
7. At 19:10, Room #14038 was accessed using the previous Visionline key issued to Mr. Shao on 19 February.
8. At 20:57, Room #14038 was checked in to Mr. Cheung Koon. At 21:05, he called to report finding unidentified luggage.
9. According to CCTV footage, at 19:10, two females and one child entered Room #14038 with three suitcases and one small bag.

Guest Name: Mr. Shen Yi Chen/Ms. Yang Gege
Room Number & Type: 15038 / KC
Stay Period: 28 Feb ~ 01 Mar, 2026
Booking Source: FIT (Fliggy)
Nationality: CN(SHA)

Guest Name: Mr.Li Hong Zhao
Room Number & Type: 27073 / TC
Stay Period: 27 Feb ~ 1 Mar, 2026
Booking Source: TELE (PD3A)
SRC Number: 7176664
Nationality: CN (SCS)

1. At 1434Hrs, GS TM#77853 received a baggage claim job (2 items, Luggage Tag#PC_MG_A84_8551) in the L1 baggage room. The job indicated the baggage was on the luggage rack at location PC_R1_S3, but the baggage could not be found.
2. Due to the large number of bags in the baggage room at that time, TM searched all the racks but still could not find the baggage (2*PC_MG_A84_8551). GS TM#77853 requested assistance from GS CMCT to locate the baggage and reported the situation to CSH/Dilly at 14:45H.
3. CSH apologized to the guests immediately and invited them to the baggage room to help them find their luggage. According to Mr. Shen and Ms. Yang, they had two pieces of luggage (a 20-inch canvas carry-on suitcase and a black backpack, which was tied together with the suitcase handle).
4. CSH with Mr. Shen and Ms. Yang to search for the luggage in the luggage room, but they still couldn't find the two pieces of luggage.
5. At 1454Hrs, GS CMCT#65798 received a called from the Londoner Grand GS Team, they explained that they had come to the Parisian GS counter to help their LG check in guest collect two pieces of luggage this morning, but the guest had just came to their counter and discovered that the luggage did not belong to them. Based on their description, it was determined that the two pieces of luggage belonged to the Parisian guests.
6. CSH immediately arranged for TM to retrieve the luggage (2×PC_MG_A_8551) from the Londoner Grand and found that two other pieces of luggage belonging to the Londoner Grand were still on the shelves in the Parisian luggage room (2×PC_MG_A84_5881, a black 20-inch suitcase and a black backpack).
7. CSH apologized to guests for the services delay again and learned during the conversation that the guest was going to Hong Kong for tourism and would be taking the hotel shuttle bus to HZMB Macao Port to Hong Kong. CSH immediately arranged the limousine service as a courtesy compensation. The guests agreed to the arrangements.
8. At 1510Hrs, GS TM assisted the guests in retrieving their two pieces of luggage from the LG Hotel back to the Parisian Hotel.
9. At 1515Hrs, the guests left the hotel by the limo.

Investigation:

1. At 0832Hrs, Mr.Li from R#27073 kept the 2 pcs of luggage (PC_MG_A84_5881) in L1 GS counter.
2. At 0929Hrs, Mr. Shen from R#15038 kept the 2 pcs of luggage (PC_MG_A84_8551) in L1 GS counter.
1. At 0945Hrs, GS TM#80677 received a job order in the Luggage room to return two pieces of luggage (luggage tag #PC_MG_A84_5881).
2. Because the TM did not verify the luggage tag numbers, two other pieces of luggage (luggage tag: PC_MG_A84_8551) that were placed on the same luggage rack were mistakenly taken to the counter for return.
3. When the GS TM arrived at the counter, he found that only the Londoner Grand GS TM was waiting for luggage. The TM did not double-check the luggage tag numbers, thus returning the two incorrect pieces of luggage (PC_MG_A84_8551) to the Londoner Grand GS TM.
4. Furthermore, GS TM#80677 did not scan and update the luggage tags and records of the two incorrect pieces of luggage. Instead, he scanned the luggage tag numbers of the correct luggage on the BHS job order, resulting in Mr. Shen and Ms. Yang being unable to find the correct luggage location update when they arrived at the counter to collect their luggage.

Follow up:

1. Learned from LG GS side, the guest, Mr.Li only requested to send back the correct luggage to him without other request after reported the issue, PM shift CS Head tried to make courtesy call to guest but can't reach. AM shift CS Head will make call again and offer service recovery next day.
2. We will share this case and brief the team. In any situation when handling luggage, always carefully check the baggage tag number, double-check it, and update the baggage status in the BHS system promptly and accurately.
3. The employee will be subject to disciplinary action.

Log was created by CSH/Dilly

-	At 1608hrs, a F1 HSKP entered room while the M1 HSKP still in room

1.	At approximately 2145H, Mr. Zhu from Room #23116 approached the Front Office lobby with his wife (Ms. Zhu, Lili) to report that the north wing guest lift suddenly displayed an “Out of Service” status while she was using it to descend from Level 23. She expressed her desire to file an official complaint.

5.	FOH/Tony explained the procedures for medical reimbursement to Ms. Zhu and advised her that she needed to pay for the medical fee first. Mr. Zhu, the main guest and husband of Ms. Zhu, became emotional and requested a meeting with senior management of the hotel.
6.	FOM/Theresa met with the guests in the lounge and offered to arrange a consultation with the Genesis doctor, which would be covered by the hotel; the guests accepted.
7.	The lift has been blocked for Facility team for further investigation. Meanwhile, CCTV footage was observed that a total of 3 guests (1M and 1F came out from Room#23152 and 1F came out from Room#23116) were trapped inside the Lift LPH-06, they entered the Lift at 2125hrs. After they leaving from the Lift LPH-06 at 2127hrs at L06, then they used H03 Lift to L1 at 2128hrs.
8.	FOH Leanne promptly made a courtesy call to the guests in Room #23152 to express concern and offer apologies.

rows.Subject: PA-723116 | Haiming Zhu | Lift Trapped in North Wing Guest Lift LPH-06
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Updated by FO/Tony on 20Mar:

Learned from R#23152 & R#23116 guest as below:
- The lift from 23th -20th floor is normal speed 
- From 20th to 6th floor run very fast
- Then from 6th floor up to 20th floor and down to 6th floor again  

CCTV review below<Security Ref no: 2603P-1966>:
1. CCTV footage that unable to confirmed the moment of the lift up & down again. 
2. CCTV footage could not confirm the speed of the lift's movement between L23- L20 and L20- L6 and the lift display panel indicated the lift moved from L6 up to L20,  then returning down to L6. 

R#23152:
1. Around 2337H,  a call was received from Ms. Wu at room 23152 requesting urgent assistance from the in-house doctor.
2. FOH/Tony approached room R#23152 and knocked on the door,  but there was no response. Later,  FOH Tony observed that Mr. Zhou and Ms. Wu exited from room R#23116. FOH Tony encountered the guest at the entrance of room R#23152,  accompanied by the EMT and FOM-Theresa.
3. Mr. Zhou claimed that he was a bit dizzy but declined doctor service. Ms. Wu was assessed,  revealing that her body temperature and blood pressure were normal by in house doctor; nevertheless,  she still felt unwell and reported experiencing minor genital bleeding,  which might be linked to an endocrine disorder.
4. The in-house doctor suggest the guest to go to hospital for additional examination; however,  the guest chooses not to go to the hospital at this time and prefers to monitor their condition independently first. No medicine was prescribed to guest. 
5. Around 1200H on 21/Marm guest request hotel call back for any required assistance regarding the hospital.
6. The guest request $50, 000 per person for Mr. Zhou and Ms. Wu (Total $100, 000) as the compensation.

R#23116:
1. At around 22:30H,  the in-house doctor arrived at the FO Lounge area to attend to Ms. Zhu,  who reported experiencing stomach pain.
2. Following a further examination,  the in-house doctor confirmed that Ms. Zhu had elevated blood pressure (approximately 160 mmHg) and a body temperature of 37.5°C. The doctor recommended that the guest proceed to a hospital for further evaluation; however,  the guest declined. The doctor subsequently prescribed medication for gastric relief.
3. Mr. Zhu and Ms. Zhu stated that they would return to their room to rest and requested that the in-house doctor return at 23:59 to reassess Ms. Zhu’s blood pressure.
4. When FOM is escorting both Mr. & Mrs. Zhu back to room,  Mr. Zhou coincidentally met both Mr. & Mrs. Zhu at lift area and added Wechat accordingly.
5. Around 0020H,  the in-house doctor arrived at room #23116 following a consultation from room #23152.
6. The in-house doctor assessed that Ms. Zhu has high blood pressure,  registering around 155 mmHg,  and recommended that she visit the hospital for further evaluation. FOM/Theresa politely explained to the guest that they need to settle the medical fee from hospital by themself first,  while the hotel will provide a limousine and a staff member to accompany her.
7. At around 01:00H on 21Mar,  Ms. Zhu was sent to Hospital Conde S. Januário which accompany with his husband (Mr. Zhu) and one of CS TM by hotel limo. 
8. At around 01:00H on 21Mar,  Ms. Zhu was sent to Hospital Conde S. Januário which accompany with his husband (Mr. Zhu) and one of CS TM by hotel limo. 
9. R#23116 Mr. Zhu mentioned that will arise a serious complaint to higher management for medical expenditures & medical imbursement procedure.


FOM communicated to the guests R#23116 and R#23152 that there is no assurance of any compensation fee,  and this matter will be referred to Risk and Management for additional investigation and follow up. 


Updated by CSH/Dilly on 21 Mar, 
1.At 03:10H,  Room#23116: Mrs. Zhu and Mr. Zhu were accompanied by CS local TM from the hospital to the hotel by limo.
2.CSH met and greeted the guests,  inquired about their specific situation,  and the guests mentioned that Mrs. Zhu had post-traumatic stress disorder and stomach cramps after being scared. However,  as Mrs. Zhu was in her pregnancy preparation period,  she could not take any medication and could only rely on self-rest for recovery. 
3.CSH provided contact information to the Mr.Zhu ,  and Mr. Zhu will contact us after waking up to handle the subsequent compensation matters,  Mr. Zhu requires communication with senior management. 
4.Mr. Zhu said that since they hadn't eaten dinner,  they were now hungry and had some stomach discomfort,  and needed some meat. CSH informed the IRD to arrange two servings of porridge,  char siu,  and roast goose send to room.

Updated by DOO/Peter at 10:30 on 21 Mar
1. Mr. Zhu showed concern about the incident happen last night which hotel delay in offer immediate response from lift trapped which happen at 21:25 and hotel team only aware the case when he approach counter for complaint at 22:30 on 20 March
2. Ms. Zhu (Wife of Mr. Zhu),  still not feeling very comfortable and not able to sleep for whole night 
3. Guest claimed that he requests further claim when he back to Shanghai for below:
•	Ruin the pregnancy plan as her wife is undergo Oocyte retrieval
•	Absent form work compensation due to treatment require in China
•	Mental claim for Ms. Zhu due to the lift trapped incident
4. DOO/Peter well explained to guest that this will further go through risk management,  and he is welcome to send us the receipt and certification for further evaluation,  DOO business card was given to guest for reference.
5. Meanwhile,  as guest is departing today,  2 pax le buffet breakfast have offered and Mr. Zhu further ask if we can offer a spa for her wife so that she can relief the stress,  DOO agreed to offer 60 mins spa as courtesy and related spa waiver form have to be signed.
