Follow up:
1.	Spa booking have been arranged at 14:00 on 21 March for Ms. Zhu Lili followed escorted by concierge team from room to L6 Spa.
2.	At 15:22,  Mr. Zhu & Ms. Zhu were bid farewell by DOO/Peter and CSM/Steven from Parisian PC to Zhuahi Airport via cross border coach (Self purchase ticket),  guest was advised to contact us in submission relevant certificate and receipts so that it can refer to risk department for further evaluation.
3.	Case shared to facility team and security team for reference and to archive related lift check report and CCTV footage.

Ms. Wu further asked for Massage and F&B arrangement from 21-Mar evening until to 22-Mar noon,  and also cash voucher for shopping as well,  FOH/Louis kindly decline to Ms. Wu’s requested,  and explained to Ms. Wu that both FOM/Jeyson and MR. rows.Incident Description:
Guest Name: Ms. Liu, Yaohong
Room Number and Room Type: 22069(TC)
Stay Period: 22 - 25 March 2026
Booking Source: Casino(Tele-PD3C)
SRC#5075645
Nationality: CN(Guangdong)

1. Around 1703H, received call from PSC mentioning that Ms. Liu from R#22069 asking for medical assistance as she had injured in room. 
2. At 1707H, FOH/Niki & EMT arrived guest room. Heard from the Ms. Liu as below: 
-The incident occurred at around 12:00H on 23 March. She was heading to open the door for the housekeeping team to provide room cleaning services when she accidentally stumbled over the door stopper (see attached photo) inside the R#22069 and fell toward the main entrance door.
-Her whole body was hit on the room entrance door, resulted in bruising, swelling, and minor scratches on her left forehead, in addition to twisting and swelling in both palms.
- She was wearing sport shoes.
- She only contacted PSC at around 13:10H to request an ice bucket but did not inform for her injury sustained in the hotel room.
- The housekeeping room attendant inquired about her wellbeing and recommended medical assistance, but she declined it, believing her situation was not serious.
- Around 17:00, she experienced dizziness and pain in her palms, prompting her to call the PSC for medical assistance.
3. The EMT assisted the guest by disinfect the wound and using an ice pack to alleviate the swelling.
4. FOH/Niki recommended that the guest undergo a follow-up examination at the hospital. The guest inquired whether the hotel could cover the medical expenses immediately, FOH politely declined and explained that the guest needs to pay for the medical fee first, and the hotel front office team would facilitate the reimbursement after receiving the medical receipt.
5. Guest decided to visit Zhuhai hospital and confirmed limo departure at 18:30H. FOH added Ms. Liu's WeChat as contact point. 
6. At 18:20H, FOH entered the room to accompany the guests for their limousine. Ms. Liu and her husband, Mr. Liu, changed their minds and insisted that the hotel cover their medical expenses rather than following the standard medical claim procedure. They also inquired whether the hotel could ensure full reimbursement of all medical fee, including potential lost income and nursing care expenses. The FOH politely explained the medical reimbursement process. The guests further claimed they lacked the money and insisted that the hotel pay the expenses directly. The FOH advised Ms. Liu that she could have a consultation at Macao Hospital first and could settle the medical fees within a month at the hospital. Ms. Liu then requested to see the higher manager in the room. The FOM/Theresa was informed at 18:37.
7. Ms. Liu and Mr. Liu repeated their request, FOM/Theresa politely informed the medical reimbursement process and kindly offered assistance with hotel transportation, proposed sending one team member to accompany the guest to the hospital and also offered dining arrangements for the guest. However, the guest declined these offers and requested to file a police report at 18:57.
8. At 19:21, one PSP arrived and met Mr. & Ms. Liu in room. 
9. Mr. Liu insisted to have a police report certificate to validate that a medical incident occurred in room #22069 of the Parisian, which was denied by PSP.
10. The PSP provided a clear explanation regarding his inability to deliver the report and invited the guest to make a statement at the police station, where they would generate a simple report documenting the guest's police report on 23 March, albeit without specific incident details. Additionally, Mr. Liu requested that the hotel issue a certificate featuring the company letterhead or with company stamp, which was declined by FOM and FOH. It was recommended that the guest visit a hospital to obtain a medical certificate from a doctor, but the guest declined.
11. At 21:15, the Guest ultimately made the decision to provide a statement at the police station.
12. At 21:50, Ms. Liu contacted the FOH to request limousines to CHCSJ hospital from police station. One CS GRO has been arranged to accompany Ms. Liu and Mr. Liu to the hospital.

Log was created by FOH/Niki

2. At 01:18H, guest called PSC to rush the job.
3. At 01:35H PSC received call from housekeeping team that guest room turned on DND light.

             Two in-house guests were trapped in Eiffel Tower Lift E02 for approximately 12 minutes, with no injuries sustained.

9. 20:51: Guests expressed gratitude for the team’s care and left the attraction without any complaints.

10. 20:52: The incident was formally reported to Front Office TM#25922.

11. Schindler is investigating the cause of the lift OOO.

12. CCTV footage for the incident is still pending.

rows.Incident Description:
1. On 30 Apr 2026, at 09:40hrs, informed by SEC, Mr. Zhu was struck by a handcart pushed by a man in red clothing on the second floor of the LO Shopping Mall. (in the front of Retail Shop HOGAN)
2. Service Assurance Manager (SAM) arrived at the scene and learnt from Mr. Zhu that he was on his way from PA to LO for breakfast this morning. When he reached the second floor of LO Shopping Mall, he was hit from behind by a handcart. Mr. Zhu stated that the handcart was moving very fast and the goods stacked on it were piled very high. After hitting him, the man pushing the cart left immediately without stopping. 
3. EMT provided first aid. Observed abrasions on the guest's right foot and left hand. Mr. Zhu claimed that he has diabetes, that his wounds heal very slowly and are prone to infection, and may has possibility of complications. SAM suggested Mr. Zhu go to hospital for professional treatment, but Mr. Zhu declined. Mr. Zhu demanded that hotel locate the man who stuck him, as he believed that man is a hotel employee, and he intended to claim compensation from that man. If hotel was unable to find the man, he demanded hotel pay compensation on the man's behalf.
4. SAM informed Mr. Zhu that hotel needed time to investigate and knowing that he had come to LO for breakfast, SAM invited Mr. Zhu and his wife to enjoy breakfast at CT while waiting for the results. Mr. Zhu declined and insisted on waiting at the scene of the incident. SAM assured the guest that hotel would not stop following up because he left the spot, we just hoped them can sit down and rest comfortably first. Meanwhile, informed by SEC that after checking the CCTV, found the man was a third-party deliver worker, had already left on a truck MX7079 at 10:09hrs. SAM informed Mr. Zhu that hotel's CCTV had captured the man, he was not a hotel employee, and he had already left the area under hotel's surveillance. If Mr. Zhu insisted on holding the man accountable, SAM suggested he report this case to the police, and hotel will assist the police on their investigation. Mr. Zhu said that if hotel would compensate him on that man's behalf, he would not call the police, since calling police at the hotel may affect hotel's reputation. SAM told Mr. Zhu that hotel supported his decision to call the police, if he insisted on finding and pursuing that man, calling the police was the best course of action. Mr. Zhu agreed to call the police.
5. While waiting for the PC officer to arrive, SEC and SAM escorted the guest to the L&F Claim room at LG Baker Tower L1 to rest. Mr. Zhu's wife was accompanying him. SAM ordered croissants and hot milk for the guests from the Conservatory as courtesy.
6. After PC officer arrived, the guests, SEC, SAM, Mall management returned to the scene together. Mr. Zhu recounted the incident once more. SEC and Mall management assisted the PC officer in locating the man. At 11:00hrs, guests went to the police station together with the PC officer.

• Casino Guest Ms. Wang Zi Xuan SRC#4789804 Diamond. She stayed in Venetian Room19047 (checkout on 19th Jan 2026). She booked for 2pax for spa treatment at 21:45 on 18th Jan 2026. She arrived at spa at around 21:00.

• Spa GRO report to spa head and immediate informed GSA to check the locker which guest had used, locker area, female changing room, spa lounge area and the treatment room.
Moreover, GSA rechecked again the used linens and bathrobes. However, we couldn’t find the 2 rings.
Spa head checked with guest’s therapist if she wear 2 rings during treatment. However, the therapist replied she didn’t wear them.
• An Email was send PA to verify, if PA team found 2 rings last time while cleaning the spa areas. PA manager replied there wasn’t any L & F report last night.
• Tim Fung had been inform to double check properly the linens which were deliver today 19th Jan 2026.
• Spa head sent email request for security team to check footage. However, they were unable to see. Case was refer to Surveillance team to check timeline when guest arrive and departure at the spa, if she had the 2 rings with her.

Investigate

• Surveillance review the footage, and saw guest was wearing the rings while playing at the table around 20:29 at NCB21859. Guest was sitting on the sofa area, unable to see on her finger when was arrive at spa. And when she approach at spa counter at 23:43, no rings were seen on her finger.

Follow up

• Host checked with guest, the price of the rings are: The BVLGARI Ring cost ¥47,700 RMB & the TIFFANY & CO. Ring cost ¥23,600 RMB.

• Case will be pass to security for further investigation.


Logged by Carl Ho

21/1/2026 Follow up by Chloe Aoieong

• As communication with marketing Sales today, Ms. Wang mentioned that she placed her two rings inside the robe before taking a shower and hung it up.

Recheck follow up

· PA team confirmed that after vacuuming last night after V SPA closed, they checked the vacuum bag for any items before discarding it.
· The laundry Timbondi also reported no findings in the linens.
· I have double checked the female’s changing room areas today including the drains, spa lounge area, the massage room where Ms. Wang was, no rings were found.

Regarding the missing rings case, Security has interviewed the female GSA last night and she has provided a written statement. We have also checked her locker together with a witness, and no suspicious findings were discovered.

rows.Incident Description:
Approximately 9:11 AM, a Ms. Du at table 21 waved to Liz, who approached the customer and asked if there was anything she could help with. Ms. Du pointed to the fried noodles in her bowl and asked if there were any eggs in the noodles. Ms. Du also told Liz that her child (around 8 years old) was severely allergic to eggs and milk and wanted to know the answer because the chef had said twice that there were no eggs in the noodles. Liz then went to the buffet line and asked Chef Leong (64574) if there were any eggs in the noodles. Chef Leong replied that there were no eggs. Liz then asked Chef Leong why the food label indicated eggs, but Chef Leong did not respond. Liz then reported the incident to the duty manager, Pong. After understanding the situation, Pong went to the customer (Du Yu Yong - Room #17090) and apologized. Ms. Du told Pong that she had noticed her son had a slight cough and had asked again whether there were any eggs in the noodles. Chef Leong had confirmed that there were eggs in the noodles. Pong confirmed that there were eggs in the noodles and asked if she needed to see a doctor, but Ms. Du refused because she wanted to observe the situation for a while. Pong offered the duty number to Ms Du in case anything happens.

Pong offered her tissues and explained that the food tag at Milan listed the ingredients of eggs. Ms. Du then said she understood. While Ms. Du returned to her seat to eat, Pong informed the front desk duty manager about the case and also informed Peter Kong. Around 10 a.m.  Ms. Du and her family were leaving, Pong approached Ms. Du to ask about her child status. Ms. Du replied that everything was fine so far, and they were going back to their room to give the child allergy medication.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Security Narrative Report:

Monetary Issue and Attempted Suicide
On 17/Feb/2026 at 0616hrs,  Priority Service Center had requested medical and Security assistance respectively for Suite 13043 (Male Registrant,  Ruby I,  Comp. Room,  Check In/Out: 15-17/Feb/2026). Security EMT and Front Office responded to the suite and found that the male registrant (M1) and a female registrant of Suite 28016 (F1,  Diamond II,  Comp. Room,  Check In/Out: 13-19/Feb/2026) inside Suite 13043. Reportedly,  F1 claimed she had a personal monetary issue of HKD 20, 000 with another male in-house guest (M2,  Ruby I) of Suite 13043 inside Gaming Floor on 16/Feb/2026 and M2 was became unreachable. F1 declined any medical assistance but requested to file a formal complaint to PJ. Security called PJ Casino hotline and referred the case to on-duty PJ. F1 and M1 were then invited to PJ corridor. Surveillance footage review showed that from 0013hrs-0027hrs,  M2 received 2 pieces of HKD 10, 000 chip from F1 nearby NCB 249/55 and started to play. At 0039hrs,  both of them left the said location and M2 eventually left the property via taxi at Main Lobby Taxi station at 0443hrs. Result was replied to relevant parties. At 0743hrs,  F1 suddenly became emotionally unstable at PJ corridor and bumped her head onto the wall several times which was stopped by Security immediately and Security verbally reminded her that this was an undesirable behavior. F1 declined any medical assistant and no injury was reported. F1 and M1 left PJ corridor after reporting without any further request. Later at 0844hrs,  Priority Service Center informed that M1 requested for Security assistance for Suite 13043 again since F1 approached his suite and was disturbing him by continuously knocking his suite door. Security and Front Office responded to the scene then a room changing service was offered to M1 by Front Office. Afterward,  F1 became emotionally unstable again and suddenly bumped her head onto the wall nearby Suite 13043 and stopped by Security. Security Control Room immediately summoned Outside PSP for assistance and dispatched EMT to the scene. Later,  outside PSP arrived and EMT provided first-aid (icepack) to F1 since she sustained redness and swelling on her forehead,  also escorting her to PJ corridor by wheelchair while PSP summoned ambulance services for F1 at West Lobby (Point E). Later,  ambulance arrived but F1 refused to go to hospital. After PSP mediation,  F1 was invited out of the interview room and returned to Suite 28016. Since F1 was previously verbally warned,  1-month barring as Undesirable Behavior was imposed on her as agreed by Concerned Departments. Eventually PSP left since no further request from F1. At 1517hrs,  Priority Service Center informed that F1 requested for PSP assistance again at Suite 28016,  Security dispatched to the Suite where the guest became emotionally unstable again and dropped the request to call PSP.  At 1600hrs,  F1 left the Suite and Security kept following her. At 1608hrs,  F1 attempted suicide by climbing over the barrier beside CE17 escalator where she was grabbed and subdued immediately by Security. She was then invited into the BOH area beside Shop L03 Retail Shop 611 (Noble Mart). Meanwhile,  SCR observed a female walk in guest had taken a video for the incident and she was later located at West Lobby bus deport where Security approached her and the relevant video was then deleted. Player Development arrived the scene while on-site PSP was notified and later 3 outside PSP arrived and PSP summoned ambulance service for the female guest. Eventually,  Paramedics arrived and used the stretcher to assist her for boarding on ambulance at LG Loading Dock. Eventually,  F1 was conveyed to Macau CHCSJ Hospital. UFO barring for Undesirable Behavior was imposed on her as agreed by concerned Departments. F1's Suite was force-checked-out and her luggage was claimed by her male companion who was checked-in with F1 on 13/Feb/2026 as approved by Front Office. Security also recommended to bar the suspect from checking-in the SCL Hotels (including partner hotels). Later at 2213hrs,  F1 alone returned to Main Lobby by Taxi and took escalator to L3. Then,  she was seen climbing over the barrier at L03 Great Hall by mall security. Macao Fire Service Department was then notified while the L03 Great Hall and L01 Rolex area were immediately cordoned by Security. At 2217hrs,  PSP and FSD arrived at the scene and set up the rescue cushions at L01. At 2234hrs,  F1 threw her mobile phone to L01 Gaming Floor and the said phone was later returned to F1,  no injury was reported. Log was updated by FOH/Winson on 21 Feb 2026

1.	At 1240H,  FOH/Winson and HSKP EH/Kasten attended the room and learnt from Mrs. Zhai who is the boy’s mother that His son crawling on the floor in room and found the straw (Photo attached) under the bed,  then he put it into his mouth and injured his throat. However,  when Mr. Zhai returned back the room and Winson heard Mr. Zhai’s sister-in-law describe the incident to Mr. Zhai as follows:
a.	The family was preparing to go out and close the door. While closing the door,  they suddenly heard the boy crying loudly. They then turned on the room light and found the boy holding an unknown straw in his hand. 
b.	They have not confirmed where the straw came from,  so they suspected the boy found it under the bed. 
2.	Mr. Zhai questioned the cleanliness and sanitation of the hotel room. Winson politely explained to guest that all room are thoroughly cleaned and inspected in accordance with our official hygiene guidelines with hotel policy before guest check in which Mr. Zhai showed understanding. 
3.	After inspected by EMT team,  there was a small indentation was found in the boy’s throat,  with no bleeding observed. EMT did not provide any first aid due to the boy is younger and suggested guest to hospital for further checkup. 
4.	At 1310H,  Winson and Security assisted the boy to West Lobby to take taxi to Taipa Kiang Wu Hospital and was accompanied by his parents. 
5.	At 1436H,  Mr. Zhai returned the call and learnt from that his boy just finished the doctor consultation. After the doctor’s examination,  it was confirmed that the boy was not seriously injured. No disinfection was performed because the boy was too young. Mr. Zhai appreciated with hotel’s assistance and did not pursue further. 

Investigation:
1.	At 2127H on 20 Feb ,  guest was checked in to room#31099 under vacant inspect. 
2.	Confirmed with CCTV review that the footage showed that at 0042H on 21 Feb,  guests entered to the suite with 1 plastic bag but unable to confirm if it was a take away food or not.

Follow up:
1. On 04 Mar,  FOH/Winson will place courtesy call to Mr. Zhai (86-153 4351 4567) to show care with guest's boy as knowing Mr. Zhai will have vacation with family in Thailand from 22 Feb.

rows.Incident Description:
On 28-Feb between 09:30 and 10:30 hrs, incorrect assignment issues occurred in FCS 1 system. Jobs created by PCS for housekeeping team were incorrectly routed to the "HSKP LDY runner" account, instead of the intended default recipient "HSKP Runner AM" account, the HSKP dispatcher was required to manually re-assign all affected jobs. The incident was reported to IT team with ticket no. INC6433109.

The IT team took immediate action, engaging the FCS 1 system vendor to investigate the root cause, conducted a system health check and reviewed backend configurations. Their initial assessment concluded that the issue was caused by human error.

On 1-Mar between 09:30 and 10:30 hrs, the issue reoccurred. It was identified that both system robot/PSC and ISD jobs intended for the HSKP team were incorrectly assigned to either the LDY account or guest service department account. The HSKP dispatcher had to perform manual re-assignment to rectify the routing. 

The issue was reported to the IT team again for further investigation, The feedback received is that the RPA team is investigating the incident, and pending for further updates from IT.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
At 03:10H on 07 Mar,  PSC informed that a male guest requested EMT assistance after sustaining an injury inside his suite. At 03:15H,  FOH staff Erik and EMT personnel rushed to the room. Details are as follows:

1. Erik expressed concern for the injured guest,  Mr. Jiang,  who is accompanying the registered guest Mr. Liu. According to Mr. Jiang,  he had placed a paper bag containing a bath towel under the light fixture near the washbasin before taking a bath. After bathing,  when he attempted to remove the bath towel from the paper bag,  his right middle finger struck the edge of the light fixture.

2. The guest’s right middle finger was cut and bleeding. Erik immediately arranged for the EMT to provide disinfection and bandaging.

3. Erik offered a sincere apology for the incident and proposed relocating the guest to another room and arranging a trip to the hospital for further checking,  but both offers were declined by Mr. Jiang.

4. Mr. Jiang stated that the edge of the light fixture was very sharp and dangerous,  and that this had caused him unnecessary injury. He further requested a one-night room charge refund as compensation. Erik acknowledged the guest’s concerns but politely declined the refund request. After learning the guests had no dining plan and intended to go sightseeing,  Erik offered alternative compensation in the form of either dining credit or limousine service. However,  the guest declined these offers and insisted on the refund.

5. The guest requested a response by 10:00H on 07 March. Pending a courtesy call to the guest.

Updated by FOH/Wayne on 07Mar:
1. At 10:00H,  FOH/Wayne placed a courtesy call to guest and showed concern for Mr. Jiang's well-being,  after obtaining the guest's permission,  Wayne and EMT rushed to room duly.
2. At 10:15H,  Wayne met guest inside room and show sincere sympathy to guest. EMT provide disinfection for guest’s wound. Wayne further offered medical assistance to go hospital for checking up but guest rejected. To create a good communication atmosphere,  Wayne invited guest to enjoy breakfast,  but it was turned down neither. Guest requested hotel to refund full stay (two nights) room charges as compensation since he already communicated with hotel last night.
3.Mr. Jiang claimed it was a serious injury to him and further expressed the staff last night didn’t care enough about him,  they only took photo and disinfected. He wasn’t even fully dressed at that time. Guest suddenly became emotional and insisted hotel to refund the full stay room charges before today,  along with an additional $1000 for mental distress otherwise he will post it to the social media.  Wayne tried to calm down guest to but guest rejected to talk any more.

Updated by FOM/Queenie @16:54H on 07Mar:
At 16:54H,  Queenie placed courtesy call to S#32033 injury guest Mr. Jiang. Queenie showed concern to Mr. Jiang as he claimed it was a serious injury to him. Queenie then suggested guest to go hospital for further check up,  and hotel will take care the medical fee. However,  Mr. Jiang himself then claimed that the hospital will do the same treatment as EMT from hotel as it is a minor cut only. Queenie politely informed Mr. Jiang that we are not able to refund him the room charge and he claimed that he will post it to the social media and cut the phone line. Before cut the line,  guest also mentioned that he doesn’t need any F&B credit or transportation arrangement.

Update by FOM/Clarence @ 18:37H on 16Mar:
FO received non-register guest Mr. Jiang complaint email regarding the incident. After discussion with management team,  offered 2*complimentary nights for guest as service recovery and email was sent to Mr. Jiang for confirmation. Guest accepted the offered and was reminded to contact FO if future plan is decided,  FO will provide necessary assistance at that time. Opera profile note has been updated in Mr. Liu's booking.

rows.Incident Description:
Guest Name: Mr. Wang Hui Wen
Stay period: 10 -20 Mar
SRC: #2528364(PD1A)

1.At approximately 09:30, Host- Henrique notified that a complaint from Mrs. Wang (Jin Ping) staying in Room 9883. Mrs. Wang was resting in the bedroom when she heard noises from the kitchen area of her room. She immediately proceeded to the kitchen to investigate and found a female TM #59738 from the Facilities, who was on the phone while pushing a trolley in the kitchen. 

2.Upon being questioned by the guest, TM #59738 promptly apologized to Mrs. Wang, explaining that she had entered the wrong room. 

3.Mrs. Wang expressed strong dissatisfaction. She questioned why any staff could access her room without authorization, stating that this made her feel extremely unsafe during her stay. She demanded a formal explanation from the hotel management. 

4.After being notified, AVP Cosimo arrived at the Mansion at 09:55 to conduct an on-site investigation. 
a. At 09:10, TM-Zhu (TM ID: #59738) from Facilities received a work order (Room 5883) requesting entry to perform painting work. 
b. Due to the elevator stopping at the 9th floor, TM mistakenly identified the target floor as the 5th floor. Without double-verifying the room number, she entered the kitchen area of Room 9883 through the back door. 
c. Upon noticing guest belongings in the kitchen, TM contacted the Housekeeping via phone to confirm the room number. 
d. Mrs. Wang entered the kitchen from the living room and questioned the TM about the unauthorized entry. TM then apologized to the guest, explaining the mistake of entering the wrong room.   

5.Given that Mrs. Wang needs to continue resting in her room, the hotel management will schedule a separate time to visit her room for an in-person apology, aiming to resolve her concerns and restore her trust in the hotel's service.
rows.Subject: 9883 | Huiwen Wang | Guest Disturbance- Unauthorized Entry
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
At 14:30,  Mrs. Wang went down to the lobby,  Head-Timmy apologized sincerely on behalf of the hotel management. He sought the guest's feedback regarding the following resolutions:

- All backdoor locks to her room will be secured. All service are strictly required to access and exit the room via the main entrance only

- No TMs are permitted to enter the room without the permission of the guest.

- Any TMs who need to access the room for any reason e.g. cleaning or maintenance must be accompanied by a butler.

Mrs. Wang agreed with the proposed solutions,  expressing appreciation for our prompt attention and handling.

AVP Cosimo arranged a hamper,  along with a box of chocolates from Churchill’s Table and a handwritten apology card to be delivered to 9883 as service recovery for the inconvenience and disturbance caused this morning.

rows.Subject: Others | - - | Paiza Hot Water Suspension Summary
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Investigation and follow up action from MEP:

1.	Root causes of the issues
•	Water leakage has occurred in the several pipe duct room due to the aging of pipework (venting valve,  pipe connection),  during the thermal contract/expansion of pipe,  which has directly led to unstable water supply. Even in the same bath room one faucet give normal hot water supply but other give insufficient hot water pressure.
•	In addition,  strong pipe flushing is conducted on the L34 simultaneously to reduce the yellow water on operational floor,  which has further reduced the overall water pressure and exacerbated the aforementioned issues.

2.	Specific Improvement Measures
•	Comprehensive Pipe Duct Room inspection: Prior to the next week of programme,  our team will conduct a thorough inspection of all pipe duct rooms during the hot water restoration,  and promptly repair any problematic parts to eliminate hidden dangers.
•	Optimize Flushing Time: We will improve the workflow and start pipe flushing earlier before the official water supply restoration. This proactive measure will effectively reduce the occurrence of yellow or turbid water.

3.	Reminder: Water Quality after Supply Restoration
•	After hot water supply is restored,  there may be a short period of turbid or yellowish water. This is unavoidable,  caused by sediment disturbance in the pipeline during water cut-off and restoration,  and it will disappear with a few minutes.
•	It is good as this practice,  the housekeeping team open hot water taps for available for a short time (says 1-2 mins) to flush the pipeline inside the guest,  Chiu can be directly reached by housekeeping team to handle abnormal situation.

Medical receipt received and will pass to related department follow up.
